subject: Renewal proposal: transient rate-lock + graduated surge credits
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <psingh@apexretail.com>, Apex Procurement <procurement@apexretail.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@apexretail.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: transient rate-lock + graduated surge credits

Hi Priya / procurement team —

Thanks again for the candid forecasting call yesterday. We read the risk you flagged around Q4 promotional spikes and the concern about being priced into sustained peak consumption. To keep the renewal moving and protect both sides, attached is an initial proposal that pairs a short-term rate lock with a graduated surge-credit mechanism. High-level: 

- 90-day transient rate lock at the current $.008/token effective on renewal sign date (prevents immediate uplift while we finalize commit levels)
- Graduated surge credits for overage above committed monthly tokens: 75% credit for first 25% overage, 50% credit for 25–50% overage, no credit thereafter; credits apply for three billing cycles to smooth the transition
- Incentive: commit uplift (12-month term) of +20% compared to last year unlocks a 6% off-list discount for the first 6 months
- Invoice timing: proposal keeps Net30 by default; we can move to Net45 for customers that need additional procurement approvals

Attachments: Apex_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet), Apex_Forecast_Surge_Model.xlsx (model we discussed).

Ask: can you confirm (1) expected PO timing, (2) whether Procurement needs Net45 or Net30, and (3) if the three-cycle credit runway is acceptable? If so, we can produce a clean SOW + DocuSign and aim to lock rates before your Q4 promo period.

I can run through the term sheet on Friday — available 10:00–11:30am PT.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: transient rate-lock + graduated surge credits

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the term sheet. A few immediate notes from procurement & forecasting: 

- PO timing: we can sign the PO by mid-September, but we need endorsement from finance for any Net45 requests (likely a 48–72 hour internal approval)
- The 90-day transient rate-lock is helpful; our main ask is clarity on how credits reconcile on invoices (gross credit applied vs. line-item rebate) — can that be a line in the SOW?
- On the commit uplift incentive: the finance team is comfortable with a conditional 12-month uplift, but they want a clear shortfall clause in case usage drops below committed levels after the first 6 months

Would appreciate if you can (1) add a shortfall protection paragraph and (2) provide an example invoice reconciliation (we can take the model and overlay our forecast).

We can do Friday 10:30am PT — please send a calendar invite.

Best,
Priya Singh
Director, Cloud Procurement — Apex Retail
psingh@apexretail.com

Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal: transient rate-lock + graduated surge credits — internal strategy

Folks — forwarding Priya's note. Quick internal posture before Friday's call: 

Key asks from customer: PO timeline (mid-Sep), Net45 gating from finance, invoice reconciliation line for credits, shortfall protection language.

Proposed counter / negotiation playbook: 
- Keep 90-day transient rate lock but make it contingent on signed PO within 21 days (protects us from open-ended lock)
- Move from three billing-cycle credits to 'three discrete billing cycles, not necessarily contiguous' (gives ops flexibility)
- For invoice credit treatment, agree to line-item credit with a single reconciliation statement per quarter (ops can implement)
- Shortfall clause: 3-month lookback with pro-rated true-up; if usage falls below 80% of committed for two consecutive quarters, client reverts to base list for remaining term (we reserve right to propose remediation credits)
- Commercial sweetener: if they sign the 12-month +20% uplift commit, provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to 25% of first month overage (capped) to help their promotional spike runbook

Attachment: internal_pricing_notes.xlsx — contains pricing scenarios and margin impacts for the three-band credit approach.

Jordan — need your legal redline on the shortfall paragraph. Diego — how feasible is the quarterly reconciliation as line-item credits from an ops/finance perspective? Alex — can you run the numbers in the attached model and show P&L against our margin thresholds.

If we keep the Net45 concession, I'd like a view of the cash flow impact (small risk but likely necessary to close).

Thanks,
Kim

Thanks for the feedback this week. Per our internal alignment, I've attached an updated clean term sheet (Apex_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf) that: 

- Preserves the 90-day transient rate lock (contingent on PO signed within 21 days of the term sheet acceptance)
- Clarifies credit treatment: line-item invoice credit with a quarterly reconciliation statement; credits show as a single line on the statement for auditability
- Adds a shortfall protection clause (3-month lookback, pro-rated true-up if committed usage drops below 80% for two consecutive quarters)
- Confirms Net45 as an acceptable invoice term when requested by finance; Net30 remains default
- Includes the onboarding overage credit (one-time, capped) when they sign the +20% 12-month uplift

Next steps:

3) Call to review: scheduled Friday 10:30–11:00am PT (I sent a calendar invite)
